subject: Re: MAP & Eval Plan — timing, ramps, and conditional SLA/discounts
messages:

Cc: carlos.ruiz@acmedata.com

Subject: MAP + SLA ask for POC and commercial timing

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re aligned internally on running a two-phase eval (sandbox pilot -> staged production canary) but procurement and infrastructure need clarity on commercial tradeoffs tied to that MAP. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood commit to a latency SLO for the canary (p50 < 80ms, p95 < 240ms) and provide a credits/discount schedule if missed?
- We’re willing to commit to a 6-month purchase if milestones are met, but need the pricing tiers and a clear ramp schedule that ties discounts to achieved MAP milestones.
- We also need a short list of telemetry/logs that prove SLO compliance for our security team.

Attaching our draft MAP and the initial eval schedule. Can you propose how Redwood would structure SLA concessions against the MAP milestones and an associated discount curve?

Best,
Amanda Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure
AcmeData Inc.

Subject: Re: MAP + SLA ask for POC and commercial timing

Amanda — great to hear you have internal alignment. Quick response and a proposed skeleton MAP and commercial tie-ins below. I’m copying Marissa (CS) and Laura (pricing) to confirm feasibility.

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Phase 1 — Sandbox pilot (2–3 weeks):
   - Objective: functional validation + perf baseline.
   - Redwood deliverables: hosted sandbox instance, initial perf report, recommended config/quantization.
   - Commercial: free trial credits; no SLA.

2) Phase 2 — Staged canary (4 weeks):
   - Objective: ramp to 10% traffic with monitoring.
   - SLO target we can commit as a pilot promise: p50 < 90ms, p95 < 260ms.
   - If p95 > 260ms for >24 hours in a rolling 7-day window, we propose a service credit mechanism (see attached SLA term-sheet) scaled to monthly committed spend.

3) Post-canary — Full commit & pricing tiers:
   - If canary achieves agreed MAP milestones (availability, latency, error-rate, ramp metrics) for 14 consecutive days, we propose a 10% onboarding discount off list pricing for the first 3 months.
   - Additional 5% discount tied to committing to a 6-month reserved capacity within 30 days of canary success.

Telemetry we will expose:
- Token-level latency histograms (p50/p95/p99)
- Per-route request IDs, KV cache hit rates, and request traces (sampled)
- Audit logs (auth events) and per-request model version metadata

Next steps:
- I’ll circulate a filled MAP workbook with milestone definitions and measurement windows by EOD.
- Laura, can you confirm the discount curve and whether the credit formula needs to be capped?

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Forwarding their MAP draft and Amanda’s asks. Quick ops note: we can provide the telemetry Amanda requested but need to lock retention windows (30/90/365 days) and whether they require raw request payloads or redacted summaries. Also, the SLO verification will need a mutually agreed runbook for dispute resolution.

Priya — do we want to make the credit pot proportional to committed monthly spend (e.g., 5% of committed monthly spend per qualifying SLO violation up to a 25% annual cap)? That keeps exposure bounded and is easy to calculate. Thoughts?

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Agree with Marissa. Proposed commercial guardrails:
- Credit formula: min( (violation_hours / hours_in_month) * committed_monthly_bill * 0.5, committed_monthly_bill * 0.25 )
- Discount milestones: 10% onboarding credit on invoice 1 if canary success; incremental 5% off if 6-month reserved commit signed within 30 days.
- Pricing hold: we can guarantee list price for 60 days from canary success to give procurement time.

Also recommended: require a joint runbook (posted to the MAP workbook) that lists measurement methodology and tie-breaker windows (UTC aligned). I’ll draft the term-sheet changes and attach for Rishi to send.

Priya
VP Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP & Eval Plan — proposed MAP workbook and SLA term-sheet

Amanda — attaching the MAP workbook and a draft SLA term-sheet that implements Priya/Marissa’s guardrails. Highlights:
- Telemetry exported: per-request latency histograms, sampled traces, and per-model version metadata. We will not export raw customer prompt text; instead we’ll provide redacted traces and token-level latency breakdowns to satisfy security.
- Credit formula (example): proportional to violation duration with a 25% monthly cap.
- Discount schedule tied to MAP milestones and signed reserved commitment.
- Measurement windows: 14-day stabilization, then 7-day consecutive success for canary acceptance.

If this looks good at a high level, we’ll produce a redline for your procurement and prepare a DocuSign link for the 6-month reserved commitment.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi / team — thanks for the fast turn. We reviewed the MAP workbook and SLA draft with procurement and infra; high-level acceptance with two asks before legal will sign:

1) Add a 30-day remediation window prior to credit payout for intermittent infra issues that are vendor-in-the-loop (we want to ensure joint remediation happens).
2) Include a clause that allows AcmeData to request a 1x performance remediation run (no charge) if p95 exceeds the target for 3 of 4 weeks during the canary.

If you can add those and send a redline, procurement will get legal engaged. We’re ready to kick the sandbox next week pending the update.

Amanda
